American Revolution and the early United States
Manhattan was at the heart of the New York Campaign, a series of major battles in the early American Revolutionary War. The Continental Army was forced to abandon Manhattan after the Battle of Fort Washington on November 16, 1776. The city, greatly damaged by the Great Fire of New York during the campaign, became the British military and political center of operations in North America for the remainder of the war.[71] The military center for the colonists was established in New Jersey.[72][73] British occupation lasted until November 25, 1783, when George Washington returned to Manhattan, as the last British forces left the city.[74]

From January 11, 1785, to the fall of 1788, New York City was the fifth of five capitals of the United States under the Articles of Confederation, with the Continental Congress meeting at New York City Hall (then at Fraunces Tavern). New York was the first capital under the newly enacted Constitution of the United States, from March 4, 1789, to August 12, 1790, at Federal Hall.[75] Federal Hall was also the site where the United States Supreme Court met for the first time,[76] the United States Bill of Rights were drafted and ratified,[77] and where the Northwest Ordinance was adopted, establishing measures for adding new states to the Union.[78]

Instead of sleeping tonight, I started designing mechanics for custom airships (and possibly other vehicles). Here is some of it:

Ships have stations based on their class and hit die.

Ship classes:
Ultralight: 1d4 hit dice, 4 stations
Light: 1d6 hit dice, 6 stations
Medium: 1d8 hit dice, 8 stations
Heavy: 1d10 hit dice, 10 stations
Juggernaut: 1d12 hit dice, 12 stations

Stations:
**Basic stations**: required on every airship.
Rudder (unmanned) - lets the ship steer. When disabled, ship only moves straight
Engines (unmanned) - lets the ship move. When disabled, ship does not move.
Envelope (unmanned) - keep the ship aloft. When disabled, ship loses altitude and can not engage, but can be targeted.
**Advanced stations**: add as ship class allows.
Grappling Harpoon (manned) - Can tether other ships reducing both ship’s movement to zero.
Artillery (manned) - Can damage other ships 100/400 3d10
Bombs (manned) - Can bomb other ships when passing directly over using engineering boon.
Special (manned or unmanned) - Special weapons or other magic devices. Customizable. Some special stations can take up more than one station slot, and require more crew to operate.
Plating (unmanned) - Plating will be destroyed in place of another station.

**Engineer** - must choose which systems to fix. 
The engineer can, as an action repair a system as long as there are supplies to do so. As bonus action, the engineer can charge a station.
Rudder - when charged, the ship’s maneuverability increases to full about face.
Engines - Dash 
Envelope - Climb. Allows the airship to climb above another ship on its next movement phase. This could be helpful to avoid collisions or drop bombs.
Grappling Harpoon - No overcharge
Artillery - Add 1d10 to damage of next shot
Bombs - Add 1d10 to bomb damage.

**Pilot** - Steers the ship
Action: Move one space forward on hex grid
Bonus Action: 
Move: Enter the station
Reaction: Dex Save DC 15 to dodge incoming attack.
Engineer’s boon: Reverse course.

**Artillery** - Blows up other ships
Action: Fire upon other ships 100/400
Bonus Action: Load special ammunition
Move: Enter the station
Reaction: ?
Engineering boon: +1d10 to damage

**Captain** - Directs fight.
Action: Activate special ability. Like cloak, ethereal jaunt, teleport, true strike, summon creature, chain lightning, or mend.
Bonus Action: ?
Reaction: ?
Move: ?

When a ship takes damage of 10 or over, roll a ship’s hit die and disable that station. A disabled station can be repaired by the engineer. If a disabled station is disabled a second time, that station is destroyed and no longer usable for the remainder of the encounter. 

Note: (What to do with station-less crew?)
Note: Ships can craft or purchase upgrades that grant special abilities. Certain upgrades are only available by Captain having good relations with factions. 
Note: Players can have proficiency in these factions, and can gain training in others. Any crew can operate a station but must pass a DC 15 intelligence check or loose any actions. A critical fail disables the system.

Keep in mind that none of this is polished, so feel free to add suggestions and improvements. I'm thinking that combat would run on a hex grid with airships maneuvering to get good attacks. When two airships are only one hex apart, ramming and boarding become options. The boarding party would probably switch to a separate channel at that point and go for normal combat rules, but maybe at 1 hex range, boarding party could also start damaging enemy ships with fireball and such.
I'm thinking that small 1d4 ships could only have one advanced station. Larger ships could have more advanced stations, and redundant basic stations to make them faster and tougher.

Making a tight knit circle of friends is normal and healthy. However, when infighting between groups of friends happens on the server, it can hurt everyone including those who have to adjudicate the dispute. It may take some time before your dms knows you well enough to know how to make your characters shine and get some spotlight. Do your best not to be upset by the fun that other people are having. We will do our best to accommodate and help make the kinds of fun you want to have happen too. The best way to accomplish this is to ask for it. Nothing is guaranteed but we can usually do our best to try to help accommodate or find a helpful compromise. If and when problems arise, we will address them.

The social contract.
We consider the game to be 75% freeplay and character driven. The other 25% belongs to your DMs to tell the story that we spent a year writing. Please do your best to keep out of character chat to the out of character channel. Additionally, there can be times when we will step in to riff and improv on the things that catch our attention. There will be plenty of time to do what we call “Invitationals.” Invitationals are enacted when a player or a DM wants to follow through on an improv story line. They can be requested by anyone, but are fulfilled only as time and DM interest allows.

It’s what my character would do. 
We love to role play. It is what we are all here to do. However, this is not an excuse to treat others as hostile or devalue them. Every other player here is a person. Even the NPCs and the descriptions of the world around you are people too. Unlike in single player video games, movies or books there is another person acting alongside you. Hiding behind the role play aspect of the game to harm players, dms or the narrative is not an excuse we can accept. Feel free to revile the villain or treat shady NPCs with suspicion. But actions such as white knighting (devaluing another players by publicly protecting them without their consent), spreading rumors or disdain for players, player characters, mods or DMs is not healthy for our community. As soon as you feel anxious about a given situation, seek help from our team. We are here to help you have fun, and to help the others around you. Fight or flight should be reserved for appropriate situations.

Most of the feed back was positive. The negative points mainly came from players who felt that they had a lack of player agency when we had to make corrections. From a top down perspective my reaction to the issues I watched as well as player feed back can be found in the new server rules. I won't post direct text here from any particular player, because that feels somewhat inappropriate. There were some complaints of favoritism and nepotism, as well as long wait times during combat. As well as some hard feeling from a couple of the players who we had to call out. Some of this is us, which is one of the reasons I asked for so many dms for next year. DM burn out is a real thing in roanoke. But some of it was also players failing to take personal responsibility for their attitudes and actions. We didn't ask anyone to leave this year when maybe we should have. It's always been my goal to try and retain people with kindness.

Some of the way the infighting happened comes down to bad game design on our part. Some of it comes down the way cliques treat each other as just part of the human condition.  And some of it comes down to how intensely players attach to their characters in our format.

What went wrong is something I've thought about often, some of my character flaws involve being blunt and wanting to fix things as soon as I perceive there to be a danger, or a situation that could end up hurting others. But on the other side of that coin, I find my self analyzing my self for faults when the folks who are doing the negative things sometimes do not.  Try to remember that though we are running a public server this is also a free service. We are volunteers giving our time in a labor of love. When that labor is met with petty squabbles, bitterness and resentment it can be tough to stay humble and keep serving. People can sometimes find themselves caught in despair or attitudes of entitlement and forget that the events happen daily because we are playing a game that tells a complete story. Sometimes they forget that this isn't a single player experience and that their characters reactions are also a player choice. And sometimes we need to remember that people are concerned about their reputation. Which is a valid concern. We are weighing between likely consequences of taking steps to intervene and the consequences of our inaction in a case by case string of choices.

Shenanigans day and the cult of castor really set a rift between people. The bipartisanship of the cliques became an echo chamber of folks taking sides and wanting to protect their friends. Offense is a stumbling block that isn't easily overcome. There were a handful of people who swung too hard either into feeling the guilt of their decisions or into feeling defensive and assuming no guilt whatsoever. That is something we can't control. All we can do is do our best regardless of unexpected fall out.
